description:
## Outcome

A clean `jido_cli` checkout resolves one approved Hex release of `jidoka`. It does not need the sibling `../jidoka` checkout.

## Why now

`mix.exs` now uses `{:jidoka, path: "../jidoka"}`. An isolated source build and every packaged release will fail without the sibling repository.

## Work

1. Select or publish the first Jidoka Hex version that contains every public API used by the completed CLI phases.
2. Replace the default path dependency with a bounded Hex requirement and refresh the relevant lock entries.
3. Keep any local workspace override explicit and development-only. The release and CI path must use Hex.
4. Add a clean-checkout check that copies or checks out only `jido_cli`, runs `mix deps.get`, and compiles without the sibling repository.
5. Keep the public Jidoka boundary test active and update contributor release instructions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mix deps` reports a Hex Jidoka dependency in the release path.
- [ ] A clean checkout with no `../jidoka` directory runs dependency resolution, compilation, tests, and docs.
- [ ] `mix.lock` contains the approved immutable package version.
- [ ] Production CLI code uses only documented public Jidoka APIs.
- [ ] No live provider credential is necessary for verification.

## Tests

Run the clean-checkout check, `mix quality`, `mix test --cover`, and `mix docs`.

## Non-goals

Do not vendor Jidoka. Do not copy private Jidoka modules into this package. Do not publish a release in this task.
title: Publish against the approved Hex Jidoka dependency
